text.p: Shares of Japan Tobacco Inc (JT) rose on the Tokyo Stock Exchange for a third consecutive session on Monday afternoon to hit a high for the calendar year, traders said.
By 0507 GMT, JT shares were up 6,000 yen at 960,000 yen.
The previous 1997 high was 959,000 yen marked on Friday.
"The entire market is falling due to a drop in New York, but investors consider JT a defensive share and it is attracting a small-lot buying," a trader at a second-tier brokerage said,

"JT shares are relatively cheap in terms of its price-to-earnings ratio. Some traders are buying the issue because the company's earnings in the non-tobacco divisions, such as anti-HIV drugs and Burger King businesses, are increasing," a trader at a large brokerage said.
